paper_title: Precision Metrology Meets Cosmology: Improved Constraints on Ultralight Dark Matter from Atom-Cavity Frequency Comparisons
notes: Paper constrains ultralight scalar dark matter coupling to electron mass (d_me) via frequency comparisons between Sr optical lattice clock, cryogenic Si cavity, and H maser. Primary results shown in Fig. 2(b) for d_me limits derived from fH/fc ratio spanning 10^-21 to 10^-16 eV. Data points extracted from Fig. 2(b) amplitude spectrum; values are approximate read-offs from the exclusion plot. The paper also constrains fine-structure constant coupling (d_e) shown in Fig. 2(a), but the pre-analysis hint and primary physics focus is on electron mass variation. Local DM density of 0.3 GeV/cm³ is explicitly stated in Eq. (6) and used in the analysis. Confidence level is 95% as stated throughout. Dynamical decoupling extension (Fig. 3) reaches higher masses (~10^-14 eV) but with lower sensitivity; main results focus on the frequency-comparison data.
